span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A generic same-different algorithm is applied unconsciously to the prime pair whatever its format, and the response it evokes then facilitates or interferes with the response demanded by the conscious target pair.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: If 'same' judgments are holistic and parallel while 'different' judgments are serial, then global-workspace theory predicts that only the parallel 'same' route can run without conscious access, so priming should come from same primes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Unconscious integration succeeds in this task because the stimuli fall within a sufficiently small spatial (and temporal) window and are of limited complexity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The review cannot say why this task succeeds where other unconscious-integration designs are unreliable.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the word version of the task primes and targets were not cleanly separated, so part of that effect may be a conscious stimulus-response mapping.

span.label: subliminal priming - an operational definition with a NUMBER in it: the prime is shown for 50 ms or less and immediately followed by masks, and awareness is treated as absent because of the timing. Set beside Hoewe2020, where unawareness is established by asking the participant afterwards, this is the same criterion secured by apparatus instead of by report
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: genuine unconscious processing - a term defined by what it must be distinguished FROM. The two criteria exist so that an effect cannot be attributed to the conscious preparation of response links, and to rule out visual similarity. The definition is a list of alternative explanations that have to be closed off
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same-different task, as a tool rather than a topic - what recommends it is a STRUCTURAL property: the judgement concerns the relation between two targets, so the primes can be drawn from an entirely different set and still bear on the response
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → the dual process model of same-different judgements and the global neuronal workspace theory of consciousness
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: primes —distinct-from→ targets
span.note: differs in: THE FORMAT THEY ARE PRESENTED IN, required to differ so that an effect cannot be explained by visual similarity between the two · strength of the relation: 0.9 — A methodological REQUIREMENT stated as a distinction - the two must be kept apart by design, which is why this literature ends up inventing tasks rather than analyses.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: criteria —part-of→ subliminal priming
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — The first criterion, and its justification is the whole content: primes must come from a large or novel set SO THAT the effect cannot be attributed to consciously prepared response links. The rule is shaped by the alternative it excludes.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: same-different —operationalised-as→ primes
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The design change that buys the separation: two masked primes and two targets side by side, and a judgement about the RELATION between the targets rather than about either one.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the subliminal same-different task, the time to judge whether two target colours matched was determined by whether two invisible digit primes matched, so the same-different judgment was carried out on the unseen primes as well.

span.label: The unconscious same-different priming effect is short-lived: it appeared at a 100 ms prime-target interval and was gone at 316 ms.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because the prime set (Arabic digits) and target set (colour patches) had nothing in common, the effect cannot be attributed to visual overlap or to consciously prepared action triggers, the two standard objections to subliminal semantic priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When the primes were an upper- and lower-case letter matched for visual similarity, the same-different judgment could only rest on letter identity, which the author treats as strong evidence for unconscious semantic processing.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The unconscious same-different judgment is context-relative: the pair 'a A' primed a 'same' response when surrounded by dissimilar primes but a 'different' response when surrounded by very similar primes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In a multimodal version pairing a visual and an auditory stimulus, unconscious integration across the senses appeared only for participants who had been given conscious training beforehand.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The subliminal version of the task reproduces the fast-same effect, in which 'same' responses are faster than 'different' responses.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The prediction that priming should be confined to 'same' primes is not borne out consistently: some experiments show priming only for same primes and others only for different primes.
